n2-set-15-q-1.translation: Eating breakfast raises body temperature that dropped during sleep, thereby enhancing concentration during the morning.
n2-set-15-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: teika / 低下 - decline, drop, decrease (体温が低下した = body temperature dropped).

choices.reason: ていか is the correct on-yomi reading of 低下 (drop/decline).
ていが incorrectly voices 下 as ga.
ていげ uses the alternative reading ge for 下, which is not used in 低下.
でいが incorrectly voices both 低 (dei) and 下 (ga).

n2-set-15-q-2.translation: Due to shoddy construction work, the house floor sinks when you walk on it.
n2-set-15-q-2.correctAnswerEnglish: shizumu / 沈む - to sink, subside, or cave in.

choices.reason: しずむ is the correct reading of 沈む, meaning to sink or give way under weight.
ひずむ means to warp or contort (歪む).
すすむ means to advance or progress (進む).
ゆがむ means to distort or warp (歪む).

n2-set-15-q-3.translation: Economic recovery is the matter of greatest concern for job-hunting students.
n2-set-15-q-3.correctAnswerEnglish: kanshinji / 関心事 - matter of concern / interest.

choices.reason: かんじんじ misreads 心 as jin.
がんじんじ incorrectly voices both 関 (gan) and 心 (jin).
かんしんじ is the correct on-yomi reading of 関心事 (matter of interest/concern).
かんじんし misreads both 心 and 事.

n2-set-15-q-4.translation: Damage to agricultural produce caused by abnormal weather is occurring across various regions.
n2-set-15-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: nousanbutsu / 農産物 - agricultural produce / farm products.

choices.reason: のうさんぶつ is the correct on-yomi reading of 農産物 (agricultural produce).
のうざんぶつ incorrectly voices 産 as zan.
のうさんもつ misreads 物 as motsu instead of butsu.
のうさくもつ is the reading of 農作物, which uses 作 rather than 産.

n2-set-15-q-5.translation: Safety standards for infant toys can never be too strict.
n2-set-15-q-5.correctAnswerEnglish: kijun / 基準 - standard, criterion, benchmark (安全基準 = safety standards).

choices.reason: きてい is the reading of 規定 (regulations/provisions).
きそく is the reading of 規則 (rules).
きじゅん is the correct on-yomi reading of 基準 (standards/criteria).
きはん is the reading of 規範 (norms/model).

n2-set-15-q-6.translation: With mental illnesses, even diagnosing the name of the illness is extraordinarily difficult.
n2-set-15-q-6.correctAnswerEnglish: shindan / 診断 - medical diagnosis (診断する = to diagnose).

choices.reason: 診断 is the correct kanji combination for medical diagnosis.
侵断 incorrectly uses 侵 (invade/infringe).
審断 uses 審 (judge/examine in court), not medical diagnosis.
信断 uses 信 (faith/believe), which is incorrect.

n2-set-15-q-7.translation: At the theater, I check large luggage and overcoats at the cloakroom.
n2-set-15-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: azukeru / 預ける - to deposit, entrust, or leave in someone's care.

choices.reason: 項ける is not a valid word; 項 is used in kou (item/clause).
預ける is the correct kanji for depositing or entrusting items to someone's custody.
領ける is not a valid word; 領 is used in ryou (territory/possession).
頂ける is itadakeru (humble form of receive, can receive).

n2-set-15-q-8.translation: That child looks truly clever / smart.
n2-set-15-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: rikou / 利口 - clever, smart, shrewd, bright.

choices.reason: 利行 does not form the word rikou.
利効 is not the kanji for cleverness; 効 means effect.
利口 is the correct kanji combination for rikou (clever/smart).
利硬 uses 硬 (hard/stiff), which is incorrect.

n2-set-15-q-9.translation: Training for new employees is conducted for one month after joining the company.
n2-set-15-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: kenshuu / 研修 - training, induction course, study (新入社員の研修 = new employee training).

choices.reason: 研修 is the correct kanji combination for kenshuu (training/study course).
検修 uses 検 (inspect), which is incorrect for employee training.
研習 uses 習 instead of 修.
検習 uses both incorrect kanji.

n2-set-15-q-10.translation: Last night at a jewelry store, goods worth 200 million yen were stolen by someone.
n2-set-15-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: nusumareta / 盗まれた - was stolen (passive form of 盗む).

choices.reason: 除まれた is not a verb; 除く is nozoku (to remove/exclude).
奪われた is ubawareta (snatched/robbed), not read nusumareta.
詐まれた is not a valid verb form; 詐 is used in sagi (fraud).
盗まれた is the correct passive form of 盗む (to steal).

n2-set-15-q-11.translation: That politician was formerly the leader of an anti-establishment movement.

choices.reason: 新体制 means a 'new regime/system', which does not fit an opposition movement (運動).
現体制 means the 'current regime/system'.
反体制 (hantaisei) means anti-establishment, forming the compound for an anti-establishment movement.
前体制 means the 'previous regime/system'.

n2-set-15-q-12.translation: The department manager is a person of great self-confidence.
n2-set-15-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: jishinka / 自信家 - person full of self-confidence.

choices.reason: 自信屋 is not standard; -屋 is used in patterns like 恥ずかしがり屋.
自信家 (jishinka) is the established Japanese noun suffix meaning a person characterized by strong self-confidence.
自信人 is not an existing word.
自信者 is not an established compound.

n2-set-15-q-13.translation: The damage from volcanic ash extended over an extensive area.
n2-set-15-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: kouhan'i / 広範囲 - wide range / extensive area.

choices.reason: 大範囲 is not standard Japanese; 広範囲 is the compound for an extensive range.
多範囲 is not a valid compound.
広範囲 (kouhan'i) is the standard compound meaning a wide or extensive range.
全範囲 means the entirety of a specified scope, not an extensive area.

n2-set-15-q-14.translation: I choose a suit that gives a favorable impression to the interviewer.
n2-set-15-q-14.correctAnswerEnglish: kouinshou / 好印象 - favorable impression / positive impression.

choices.reason: 良印象 is not standard; the prefix compound is 好印象, while 良 modifies as 良い印象.
好印象 (kouinshou) is the established compound meaning a favorable or positive impression.
優印象 is not a compound.
善印象 is not a compound.

n2-set-15-q-15.translation: He spent most of his boyhood overseas.
n2-set-15-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: shounenki / 少年期 - boyhood, juvenile period.

choices.reason: 少年期 (shounenki) is the established compound for the stage or period of boyhood.
少年代 is not standard; 年代 or 10代 uses 代, but not 少年代.
少年性 means boyish nature or qualities, not a chronological era of life.
少年時 is occasionally used in literary verse, but 少年期 is the standard term for life stages.

n2-set-15-q-16.translation: When the unemployed increase, crime also increases. In short, it can be said that economic recession is the cause of crime.
n2-set-15-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: yousuru ni / ようするに - in short, in summary, to sum up.

choices.reason: ようするに (in short / in summary) sums up the preceding premises into a concise conclusion.
そういえば means 'come to think of it', recalling an associated thought.
おたがいに means 'mutually' or 'to each other'.
ようやく means 'finally' or 'at long last'.

n2-set-15-q-17.translation: Ever since childhood, I was good at repairing broken toys and assembling things.
n2-set-15-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: shuuri / 修理 - repair, fixing, mending (machines, toys, tools).

choices.reason: 訂正 means correcting written text or speech errors.
修正 means amending or revising policies, plans, or images.
修理 (shuuri) is the standard word for fixing or repairing damaged physical objects like toys or machinery.
治療 means medical treatment or cure for illness or injury.

n2-set-15-q-18.translation: Prevailing through fierce competition, I managed to find employment at a popular company.
n2-set-15-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: kachinuite / 勝ち抜いて - winning through, surviving fierce competition.

choices.reason: 打ち抜いて means punching or piercing through physically.
出し抜いて means outwitting someone or getting the jump on them slyly.
引き抜いて means headhunting or scouting someone away from another company.
勝ち抜いて means prevailing through multiple stages of fierce competition (狭き門を勝ち抜く).

n2-set-15-q-19.translation: A computer virus unlawfully infiltrated the network.
n2-set-15-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: shinnyuu / 侵入 - intrusion, trespass, infiltration (不正に侵入する = unlawfully breach/intrude).

choices.reason: 進入 means entering a physical passage or road (e.g. 進入路), without the illicit breach sense.
侵入 (shinnyuu) specifically denotes unlawful or hostile intrusion and breach, matching 不正に.
加入 means joining an organization, service subscription, or insurance policy.
移入 means importing or transferring species/goods into an ecosystem.

n2-set-15-q-20.translation: Valuing interpersonal connections, he is a person well-suited to the role of team coordinator.
n2-set-15-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: fusawashii / ふさわしい - appropriate, suitable, well-suited (まとめ役にふさわしい).

choices.reason: うらやましい means enviable or jealous.
にくらしい means hateful or irritatingly clever.
なつかしい means nostalgic or dearly remembered.
ふさわしい means well-suited or fitting for a particular role or position.

n2-set-15-q-21.translation: The experience of accomplishing a difficult job by myself became a positive asset in my life.
n2-set-15-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: purasu / プラス - a plus, benefit, or asset (人生のプラス = a plus in life).

choices.reason: アップ means increase or improvement (e.g. スキルアップ), but does not fit 人生のアップ.
ダウン means decline or downturn.
プラス (plus) is commonly used as a noun meaning an advantage, asset, or valuable gain.
ダブル means double.

n2-set-15-q-22.translation: The reason this company is popular among women is that daycare facilities are fully provided, allowing them to work while leaving their children.
n2-set-15-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: kanbi / 完備 - fully equipped, fully provided (託児所が完備され = daycare fully provided).

choices.reason: 設備 is a noun meaning equipment or facilities; one does not say 託児所が設備される.
完備 (kanbi) means fully furnished or equipped with necessary amenities (託児所が完備され).
建設 means physical construction of buildings.
整理 means organizing, tidying up, or sorting out.

n2-set-15-q-23.translation: There are many people whose awareness of cybercrime is faint / insufficient.
n2-set-15-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: fujuubun na / 不十分な - insufficient, inadequate; matches 薄い (weak/insufficient awareness).

choices.reason: 不十分な means insufficient, accurately paraphrasing 薄い when describing inadequate awareness.
不正確な means inaccurate or imprecise.
不明な means unclear, unknown, or unidentified.
不透明な means opaque or lacking transparency.

n2-set-15-q-24.translation: Every time I listen to this song, I associate it with / picture the flowing of a river.
n2-set-15-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: omoiukaberu / 思い浮かべる - to picture, imagine, or bring to mind; matches 連想する.

choices.reason: 思い当たる means to hit upon an idea, suddenly realize, or think of someone/something matching a description.
思い上がる means to become conceited or arrogant.
思い浮かべる means to visualize or bring to mind, directly capturing the associative imagery of 連想する.
思い出す means to recall a past memory, whereas 連想 is an associative mental image.

n2-set-15-q-25.translation: I have prepared so that I can carry out my belongings in the unlikely event an earthquake strikes.
n2-set-15-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: moshimo / もしも - in case, if, in the unlikely event; matches 万一 (man'ichi).

choices.reason: だから means therefore or for that reason.
やがて means before long or eventually.
どんな means what kind of.
もしも means 'if by any chance / in the event that', matching 万一 in setting up a hypothetical contingency.

n2-set-15-q-26.translation: Senior Kimura meddles in our club activities over every single detail.
n2-set-15-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: komakaku / 細かく - minutely, about every little detail; matches いちいち.

choices.reason: 細かく (in detail / minutely) captures the nuance of いちいち口を出す (interfering in every single particular).
少しは means a little bit, the opposite of meddling incessantly.
最初から means from the beginning.
勝手に means arbitrarily or without permission.

n2-set-15-q-27.translation: This year, traffic accident fatalities are increasing at a record pace.
n2-set-15-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: peesu / ペース - pace, rate, speed; matches 速度 in this trend context.

choices.reason: ベース means base or foundation.
ペース (pace) is the loanword for the rate or speed at which an ongoing development progresses, matching 速度.
メーター means a measuring meter or gauge.
パーセント means percentage.

n2-set-15-q-28.translation: They say he failed in business and is now living a miserable life.
n2-set-15-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: mijime / みじめ - miserable, wretched, pitiful (e.g. みじめな生活).

choices.reason: For tragic news of a close friend's death, 悲しい (sad) or 痛ましい (painful/tragic) fits; みじめ describes wretched destitution or humiliation.
For an unhappy or pained look from a mother, 悲しそうな or 苦々しい顔 fits; みじめな顔 is not natural here.
みじめな生活 correctly describes a wretched, destitute, and pitiful existence following bankruptcy.
For moral decline or societal deterioration, 嘆かわしい (deplorable/lamentable) fits, not みじめなこと.

n2-set-15-q-29.translation: The condition of the car's engine is bad, and it is making a strange noise.
n2-set-15-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: guai / 具合 - condition, state of functioning (e.g. エンジンの具合が悪い).

choices.reason: For economic conditions, 景気 (business climate) or 経済状況 fits; 経済の具合 is unnatural.
For one's mental clarity, 頭の働き or 気分 fits; 頭の具合 is not natural.
For the state of politics, 政治状況 or 政治の情勢 fits; 政治の具合 is incorrect.
エンジンの具合が悪い is the standard idiom for a mechanical device's operating condition being faulty.

n2-set-15-q-30.translation: With such naive thinking, you won't be able to make your way through the world.
n2-set-15-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: yononaka / 世の中 - society, the world, life in society (世の中を渡る = navigate the world).

choices.reason: For waking up in the middle of the night, 夜中 (yonaka - the dead of night) is meant, not 世の中 (society).
For the animal kingdom, 動物の世界 (animal world) fits, not 動物の世の中.
世の中を渡っていく is the established idiom meaning to make one's way through human society and survive life's harsh realities.
For entering the political realm, 政界 or 政治の世界 fits, not 政治の世の中.

n2-set-15-q-31.translation: This radio has severe static/noise, so it is hard to make out the voices.
n2-set-15-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: zatsuon / 雑音 - static, noise interference, extraneous audio noise.

choices.reason: For road construction racket, 騒音 (souon - loud environmental noise) fits, not 雑音.
雑音 correctly denotes electronic static or background interference obstructing an audio signal on a radio.
For loud aircraft roaring near an airport, 騒音 (aircraft noise) is the correct term.
For complaining about minor things, 愚痴 (guchi) or 小言 (kogoto - scolding) fits; one does not say 雑音を言う.

n2-set-15-q-32.translation: In order to expand our overseas business, we are recruiting employees.
n2-set-15-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: kakuchou / 拡張 - expansion, enlarging the scale/scope of operations.

choices.reason: For a rumor spreading quickly, 広まった or 拡散した fits, not 拡張.
海外事業を拡張する correctly uses 拡張 for expanding the scale, scope, or operations of a business.
For a wide panorama opening up before one's eyes, 広がった (spread out) fits, not 拡張した.
For enlarging a photo, 拡大 (kakudai - enlargement of an image) fits, not 拡張.

n2-set-15-q-33.translation: Staking our school's reputation as a 'baseball powerhouse', I earnestly want our school to win the championship.
n2-set-15-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: kakete mo / かけても - staking / putting on the line (名前にかけて = staking one's name/prestige).

choices.reason: とっても means 'even for' or 'even if taken', which does not express putting prestige on the line.
かけても (from ～にかけて) means staking or risking something of great value, such as honor or reputation (名前にかけて).
ついても means 'concerning / regarding' (について).
よっても means 'depending on' or 'by means of' (によって).

n2-set-15-q-34.translation: Even though he is extremely wealthy, he is stingy and rarely pays money that he ought to pay.
n2-set-15-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: kuse ni / くせに - despite / even though (expressing blame or criticism).

choices.reason: せいで indicates a negative cause ('because of'), which does not contrast wealth with stinginess.
ために expresses purpose or reason, which makes no sense here.
くせに expresses critical reproach: despite having the status of a wealthy person, he is unexpectedly stingy.
あまり expresses excess leading to an extreme result ('out of excessive...').

n2-set-15-q-35.translation: Seeing her son's face for the first time in 10 years, the mother hugged him without caring about the public gaze.
n2-set-15-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: mo kamawazu / もかまわず - without minding / without caring about (人目もかまわず).

choices.reason: によらず means 'regardless of' (e.g. 昼夜によらず), not ignoring social gaze in the moment.
にかかわらず means 'regardless of / irrespective of', which lacks the personal emotional defiance of 'not minding people looking'.
を問わず means 'regardless of / open to all' (e.g. 年齢を問わず).
人目もかまわず is the fixed idiom meaning heedless of public gaze, caring nothing for people watching.

n2-set-15-q-36.translation: The moment he lit the cigarette, the room exploded with a loud bang.
n2-set-15-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: hi o tsuketa / 火をつけた - lit (past tense required before とたんに).

choices.reason: 火をつけている uses the progressive form, which cannot precede the instantaneous trigger pattern とたんに.
火をつける uses the dictionary form; とたんに strictly requires the past -た form of a punctual verb.
火をつけそうな means 'seeming about to light', which does not fit the completed trigger.
火をつけた is the required past -た form before とたんに, denoting that the explosion occurred immediately after lighting.

n2-set-15-q-37.translation: Regarding this matter, I cannot answer until I have confirmed with my supervisor.
n2-set-15-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: kara de nai to / からでないと - not unless / only after (verb-て + からでないと).

choices.reason: てからでないと followed by a negative predicate means 'unless ... is done first, one cannot ...'.
からすると means 'judging from / from the perspective of'.
からといって means 'just because ... (does not mean)'.
からして means 'judging even from / starting with'.

n2-set-15-q-38.translation: In a house covered all over in garbage like this, I am too embarrassed to invite guests.
n2-set-15-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: darake / だらけ - full of, covered with (undesirable things like trash, mud, or mistakes).

choices.reason: ごみだらけ expresses being covered all over with unpleasant or messy things (garbage).
ごみばかり emphasizes that almost everything is trash, but だらけ is the standard expression for messiness covering a space.
ごみだけ simply limits to only garbage, lacking the qualitative messiness of だらけ.
ごみのみ is a formal delimiter meaning exclusively garbage.

n2-set-15-q-39.translation: Rather than calling this wine, it tastes more like grape juice.
n2-set-15-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: to iu yori / というより - rather than ... / more like B than A.

choices.reason: というより expresses 'rather than saying X, it is more like Y', perfectly contrasting wine with grape juice.
としたら sets up a hypothetical condition ('if we assume that...').
とするなら also sets up a conditional supposition ('if we suppose that...').
といっては introduces a topic or criticism ('if one says...').

n2-set-15-q-40.translation: If it is for money, that man could very well betray even his friends.
n2-set-15-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: kanenai / かねない - might very well / capable of (doing something bad).

choices.reason: かねる means cannot / finds it difficult to do, which is the opposite of likely betrayal.
かねない attaches to a verb stem to mean 'is quite capable of doing / might well do' an undesirable action.
きれる means to do completely or finish, which is not an auxiliary expressing potential danger like this.
きれない means cannot do completely.

n2-set-15-q-41.translation: If you keep wearing clothes that are wet from the rain, you will catch a cold. Change quickly.
n2-set-15-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: nureta mama no / ぬれたままの - remaining wet / left wet.

choices.reason: ぬれたままの captures the state of clothes remaining wet without being changed.
ぬらしたきりの is unnatural; -きり typically applies to actions left after a single occurrence (e.g. 出かけたきり).
ぬれたばかりの means 'just got wet', which emphasizes recency rather than leaving them on persistently.
ぬらされたものの means 'although they were gotten wet', which does not modify 服 properly here.

n2-set-15-q-42.translation: If days without rain continue any longer, there is a serious risk that the water supply will be cut off.
n2-set-15-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: naru osore ga aru / なるおそれがある - there is a fear/risk of (an adverse event occurring).

choices.reason: なりっこない expresses absolute impossibility ('there is no way it will become'), which contradicts the drought warning.
ならずにはいられない means 'cannot help becoming', expressing irresistible psychological urge, inapplicable to water cuts.
なるおそれがある expresses a serious fear or danger of a negative event happening (断水になるおそれがある).
なるともかぎらない means 'it does not necessarily mean it will become', expressing skepticism rather than a danger warning.

n2-set-15-q-43.translation: A: 'My name is Ito, and I should have a reservation for two tonight.' B: 'Mr. Ito, is that correct? Yes, we indeed have your reservation.'
n2-set-15-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: irasshaimasu ne / いらっしゃいますね - are (honorific of である; 伊藤様でいらっしゃいますね).

choices.reason: 伊藤様でいらっしゃいますね is the standard honorific formula used by hospitality staff to confirm a guest's identity.
おっしゃいますね is the honorific of 言う (to say), which does not fit confirming a person's name with で.
申されますね mixes humble 申す with passive honorific, which is ungrammatical and incorrect.
おられますね is the honorific/polite of いる, but to confirm someone's identity ('are you Mr. Ito?'), でいらっしゃる is required.

n2-set-15-q-44.translation: You are really short-tempered, so if you feel like you are about to lose your temper at the other person, first slowly count from 1 to 10 and calm down.
n2-set-15-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: ni okorisou ni nattara / に怒りそうになったら - if you find yourself about to get angry at (the other person).

choices.reason: を怒らせそうになったら would mean if you are about to make the other person angry, but the advice is for the listener's own short temper.
相手に怒りそうになったら correctly identifies the listener getting angry at the other person (相手に怒る).
が怒られそうになったら uses an incorrect particle が and passive, suggesting the other person being scolded.
が怒りそうにしたら describes observing the other person looking angry, not controlling one's own temper.

n2-set-15-q-45.translation: Feeling unwell, I went to the hospital, but after being kept waiting terribly long, the examination was over in an instant, and I was told, 'It's just a cold.'
n2-set-15-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: ageku ni / あげくに - in the end after (a tedious or distressing ordeal); option 3 sits at the star in 'さんざん 待たされた あげくに 診察はすぐ'.

choices.reason: 待たされた follows さんざん to describe being kept waiting terribly long, placing it 2nd.
診察はすぐ modifies 終わり ('the exam ended immediately'), placing it 4th.
あげくに follows the ordeal 待たされた to mean 'only to end up in...', placing it 3rd at the star.
さんざん modifies the long wait 待たされた, placing it 1st.

n2-set-15-q-46.translation: Even he, who was said to be sarcastic and cold, was always gentle toward children.
n2-set-15-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: kodomo ni / 子どもに - toward children; option 2 sits at the star in '言われる 彼も 子どもに 対しては'.

choices.reason: 彼も is the subject qualified by the reputation, placing it 2nd after 言われる.
子どもに begins the target phrase 子どもに対しては ('toward children'), placing it 3rd at the star.
対しては completes the prepositional phrase 子どもに対しては, placing it 4th.
言われる modifies 彼 ('he, who is said to be...'), placing it 1st.

n2-set-15-q-47.translation: At this company, anyone can take the employment exam regardless of whether they are a new graduate or already graduated.
n2-set-15-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: kisotsu ka o / 既卒かを - or already graduated; option 1 sits at the star in '新卒か 既卒かを 問わず 採用試験を'.

choices.reason: 既卒かを pairs with 新卒か to form the alternatives before 問わず, placing it 2nd at the star.
新卒か begins the alternative pair 'new graduate or...', placing it 1st.
問わず follows を to mean 'regardless of whether...', placing it 3rd.
採用試験を is the direct object of 受けることができます, placing it 4th.

n2-set-15-q-48.translation: Prior to the new educational method being implemented, it was decided to test it at a small number of schools.
n2-set-15-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: sakidachi / 先立ち - prior to / beforehand (に先立ち); option 4 sits at the star in '実行されるのに 先立ち 少数の学校で 試してみる'.

choices.reason: 実行されるのに begins the prepositional clause 'prior to being implemented', placing it 1st.
試してみる modifies ことになった ('decided to test'), placing it 4th.
少数の学校で designates the location of the trial, placing it 3rd.
先立ち completes the grammar pattern に先立ち ('prior to'), placing it 2nd at the star.

n2-set-15-q-49.translation: Although it is unlikely that a veteran guide of Kimura's caliber would lose his way, let's call the police just in case.
n2-set-15-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: arumai ga / あるまいが - surely would not happen, but...; option 1 sits at the star in '道に迷う ことなど あるまいが 一応'.

choices.reason: あるまいが expresses the strong negative conjecture ('there surely wouldn't be... but'), placing it 3rd at the star.
道に迷う ('losing one's way') describes the event, placing it 1st.
一応 ('just in case') modifies the concluding proposal 警察に電話しよう, placing it 4th.
ことなど nominalizes the action 道に迷う with the dismissing nuance 'such a thing as', placing it 2nd.

n2-set-15-q-50.translation: However, contrary to expectations, the ones who most accurately guessed who was lying were those who paid attention to hand movements.
n2-set-15-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: yosou ni hanshi / 予想に反し - contrary to expectations (introduced by ところが).

choices.reason: 予想通りに means 'as expected', which contradicts ところが ('however') and the fact that few people paid attention to hands.
予想に反し ('contrary to expectations') correctly explains the surprise: although few looked at hands, that group had a 90% success rate.
予想に基づいて means 'based on predictions', which does not make sense in this context.
予想にかかわらず means 'regardless of predictions', which fails to convey the contrary outcome.

n2-set-15-q-51.translation: From the above data, we understand that one's true feelings are most easily revealed in the movement of hands and feet.
n2-set-15-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: teashi no ugoki / 手足の動き - movement of hands and feet.

choices.reason: 話の内容 (content of speech) yielded fewer correct guesses in the experiment.
顔の表情 (facial expressions) had less than half correct answers, disproving it as a reliable indicator.
手足の動き (movements of hands and feet) is supported by the data showing that hand and foot movements had the highest accuracy (up to 90%).
目の動き (eye movements) is not the top indicator revealed by the experimental findings.

n2-set-15-q-52.translation: The face, like words, can produce expressions different from one's true feelings in response to the situation of the moment.
n2-set-15-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: ni oujite / に応じて - according to / in response to (その場の状況に応じて).

choices.reason: その場の状況に応じて means 'in accordance with / depending on the situation at hand', explaining how people adjust expressions appropriately.
に関して means 'regarding / concerning', which does not express adapting expressions to match situations.
に際して means 'on the occasion of', which does not fit an ongoing situational adaptation.
をめぐって means 'concerning / centered around (a dispute)'.

n2-set-15-q-53.translation: However, telling lies (social pretense) is extremely important for maintaining human relationships.
n2-set-15-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: uso o tsuku / うそをつく - telling lies / social pretense (essential for maintaining harmony).

choices.reason: うそをつく (telling lies) is the thesis: diplomatic social lies (such as complimenting unfitting clothes) preserve relationships.
うそをつかない means not telling lies, which contradicts the explanation that expressing one's true mind would destroy relationships.
本心を語る means speaking one's true feelings, which the author explicitly states would break relationships (こわれてしまいます).
正直に言う means speaking honestly, which the author states is not always appropriate.

n2-set-15-q-54.translation: ...Even if you think someone's clothes don't suit them, you normally say 'It looks nice on you.' Being honest is not necessarily always right.
n2-set-15-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: tadashii wake de wa arimasen / 正しいわけではありません - is not necessarily the case that it is right.

choices.reason: 正しいはずがありません means 'it cannot possibly be right', which is an overly extreme total negation.
正しいに相違ありません means 'it is certainly right without a doubt', which contradicts the point about social white lies.
正しいと決まっています means 'it is established that it is right', which also directly contradicts the author's argument.
正しいわけではありません ('it is not necessarily right') completes the partial negation 必ずしも...わけではない, concluding the essay.
